_readme: Copy this file to data/search_config.json and fill it in (the /onboard skill does this for you).
This file holds every pipeline tuning knob: what to search, what to filter out, and how much
autonomy the system has. Identity and screening answers live in application_profile.json;
career goals and scoring preferences live in job_goals.json.

tracker._options: local = zero-setup tracker in data/tracker.json with a data/tracker.csv view you can open in Excel/Numbers/Google Sheets. notion = a Notion Jobs Database (needs NOTION_API_KEY and NOTION_JOBS_DB_ID in .env).

autonomy._options: search = discover and score roles only, human applies. tailor = also produce tailored CVs, human submits. full = end-to-end automated applications.

candidate._comment: Short factual summary used in deterministic and LLM realism filters. Keep it honest: it is used to REJECT roles you cannot credibly get.
candidate.summary: Alex Example, 3 years total experience (2023 - present), currently a Business Analyst at ExampleCorp in Toronto. Strong SQL, Python and stakeholder management; no people-management experience.
candidate._home_countries_comment: Countries where you already have the right to work without sponsorship.
candidate._right_to_work_labels_comment: Phrases that identify YOUR option on 'What is your work authorisation?' radio buttons.
candidate._needs_sponsorship_comment: Countries you would need a visa for. Roles there are only kept if the JD suggests sponsorship is possible; hard-gated forms get skipped or escalated.

search._comment: Named locations (with LinkedIn geo IDs from the geoId= URL parameter of a manual LinkedIn search) and named query phrases. defaults are what /auto-apply --discover uses when no flags are given.
search._watchlist_comment: Optional: career-board URLs to check beyond LinkedIn (Ashby, Greenhouse, Lever company boards). Any single posting can also be run ad hoc with /auto-apply <url>.

filters._comment: Deterministic pre-filters applied before any LLM sees the role. Empty lists disable a filter. Patterns are case-insensitive substrings unless prefixed with 're:' for regex.
filters._title_whitelist_comment: If non-empty, at least one entry must match the title.
filters._company_blacklist_comment: Companies never to apply to, e.g. your current employer and its subsidiaries.
filters._seniority_comment: A JD asking for N years is kept while N <= your variant cap + tolerance (see cv/variants/seniority_caps.json).
filters._required_language_comment: If a JD requires a language not in this list, the role is skipped.
filters._skip_contract_types_comment: Contract types to skip. Examples: internship, apprenticeship, stage, alternance, VIE.
filters._home_location_patterns_comment: Extra location substrings treated as home (city names, regions) in addition to the home_countries names.
filters._lacking_skills_comment: Skills or languages you clearly lack; JDs demanding years of them get skipped, e.g. ["java", "kubernetes"].

cv._backend_options: How your CV is produced. pdf = you supply a finished cv/master.pdf, used as-is for every application (no tailoring, zero dependencies). docx = you supply cv/master.docx and the system tailors a copy per role (needs python-docx; a PDF render of the master at cv/output/master.pdf is preferred for uploads when available). latex = the full variant system in cv/variants/ with per-role tailoring and page-fill checks (needs a LaTeX distribution).
cv._comment: default_variant applies to the latex backend only: which variant to use when no rule matches. Variants live in cv/variants/ and are generated during onboarding.

notion._comment: Database IDs live in .env (NOTION_API_KEY, NOTION_JOBS_DB_ID). These are display labels the pipeline writes into the Location select column, keyed by country.

notifications._comment: Used by run_notify.py for end-of-run emails and desktop notifications. Leave email empty to disable. Gmail needs an app password in GMAIL_APP_PASSWORD or ~/.config/jobhunter/gmail_app_password.
notifications._alert_senders_comment: Optional extra job-alert email senders for /check-emails, e.g. ["welcometothejungle.com", "careers@somebank.com"].
